title: Theories and axiomatization: sentences and model classes

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory

summary: Distinguish axioms from their consequences, characterize complete theories by agreement of their models, and test finite axiomatizability using complements.
abstract: An infinite set satisfies a separate requirement for each finite number of distinct elements. Could a finite list of first-order axioms describe exactly the same structures? Compactness shows that it cannot. More generally, a class and its complement can both be described by first-order axioms exactly when a finite list describes the class. This concerns how we specify the models, rather than how much they agree. A satisfiable theory is complete when all its models give the same answers to sentences, even though those models may have different sizes. Distinguishing the chosen axioms, their consequences, and their models makes these two questions precise.
